title: [CQ-F04b] Delete revision-less human approval compatibility
description:
Objective: Implement the human decision recorded on F04 (task-076a0bd3, comment-656dc8f8, 2026-10-25), "we dont need legacy and legacy should be deleted", for human plan approvals. Every human approval route (WS APPROVE_TASK, UPDATE_TASK AWAITING_APPROVAL->WORKING, board drag) must require the rendered expectedPlanRevision; omission is refused rather than accepted as legacy. Existing audit history stays: approvals recorded without a stamp are never deleted, upgraded or inferred.

Why a separate row: F04 was re-planned to deliver its own DoD (durable numeric approvedPlanRevision, CAS, strict-profile omission guard) with NO new legacy machinery and no deletion. The epic rails still say "Preserve legacy behavior" / "Preserve legacy policy", so deleting the revision-less path needs a human-approved MODIFY_RAIL first (governor ruling msg-74b0b3fd).

Preconditions before planning:
(1) The human-approved MODIFY_RAIL proposal on CQ-F, plus any other affected CQ epic, names exactly what may be deleted.
(2) The human has answered the scope question the governor raised: revision-less approval compatibility only, or also legacy execution/delivery profiles. If profiles are in scope, they belong to separate M-epic rows, not this one.
If either is missing, report_blocked naming the proposal or question instead of planning deletion.

Known legacy pins this row must revise deliberately (never silently weaken):
- planApproval.test.ts:
  - 'approves with no token at all (legacy caller)';
  - 'accepts an explicit 0 for a legacy row that has no stored revision';
  - 'approves when the key is omitted (legacy wire opt-out)';
  - '... (legacy board drag)';
  - 'does not use a stale token hidden in updates when the top-level key is omitted'.
- planApproval.integration.test.ts:
  - 'still approves a legacy stamp-less row when the client omits the token entirely';
  - 'moves a legacy stamp-less row off the effective 0 ...'.
- The HELD-OUT state/approvalRevision.acceptance.test.ts 'legacy missing revision remains effective zero for explicit approval' needs explicit human sign-off.

Token-omitting clients must be handled, JetBrains first (drag / Approve), then VS Code, so no supported client silently loses approval. Split client work into I02/I04-style rows if needed. Token-free daemon producers stay with their owners: relaxed set_task_status PLAN_APPROVED, and SPEED/TURBO automatic approvals in F05 (task-c7d520ba).

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve existing dirty bytes and audit history. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test (plus cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test, and the VS Code tests, if client code changes)
definitionOfDone: Every human approval route refuses an omitted plan revision with INVALID_INPUT and writes nothing (task bytes, activity, broadcast unchanged).
Existing unstamped approvals remain audit history: nothing is deleted, upgraded or inferred as a checked approval.
Every changed legacy-pin or held-out test cites the human-approved MODIFY_RAIL; no supported JetBrains/VS Code approval action loses approval without an actionable refusal.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 (plus client suites when client code changes) and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.
Plan deletion only after a human-approved MODIFY_RAIL on CQ-F names exactly what may be deleted; until then report_blocked instead of planning.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/server/planApproval.test.ts:
- 'approves with no token at all (legacy caller)' becomes a refusal: approve('task-1') with no token rejects with INVALID_INPUT naming expectedPlanRevision. The task file bytes are unchanged, status stays AWAITING_APPROVAL, there is no PLAN_APPROVED activity and no approvedPlanRevision.
- 'approves when the key is omitted (legacy wire opt-out)', for APPROVE_TASK without the key, and '... (legacy board drag)', for UPDATE_TASK {status:'WORKING'} without the key, each become an ERROR frame with INVALID_INPUT. The row is unchanged, and a second connected client receives no TASK_UPDATED.
- 'does not use a stale token hidden in updates when the top-level key is omitted' still proves the hidden token is never used. The outcome is now an INVALID_INPUT refusal instead of a legacy approval.

In planApproval.integration.test.ts, 'still approves a legacy stamp-less row when the client omits the token entirely' becomes: an omitted token is refused with no approval event, and the same stamp-less row is then approved by an explicit 0.

In WebSocketServer.test.ts:
- `${route} preserves unnegotiated %s omission` becomes `${route} refuses unnegotiated %s omission without side effects`: refused with INVALID_INPUT, status unchanged, no approvedPlanRevision.
- In 'keeps incapable sockets isolated, locked, and reset only by reconnect', the reconnected socket's final approval now sends approval('APPROVE_TASK', 4), so the test still proves that reconnect resets the lock.
- Any other token-free approval in these three files that is only setup passes the explicit stored revision.

KEEP UNCHANGED, because an explicit 0 is not an omission (architect-473624b4's comment on this task):
- 'accepts an explicit 0 for a legacy row that has no stored revision';
- 'an explicit 0 on a legacy stamp-less row authorizes revision 0';
- 'moves a legacy stamp-less row off the effective 0 ...';
- the HELD-OUT state/approvalRevision.acceptance.test.ts 'legacy missing revision remains effective zero for explicit approval'. It does not need the human sign-off its description mentions, because it is not edited.

Run the three files and confirm the flipped tests FAIL against current code for the stated reason.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT THE REFUSAL in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/taskStore.ts approveTask.

Only the two /ws human routes call state.approveTask: APPROVE_TASK, and UPDATE_TASK AWAITING_APPROVAL->WORKING (the board drag), at WebSocketServer.ts around lines 531 and 656. Relaxed moe.set_task_status and the SPEED/TURBO automatic approvals (CQ-F05) never reach it, so they stay token-free with their owners, as the description requires.

After the existing status check, add: if expectedPlanRevision === undefined, throw invalidInput('expectedPlanRevision', <fixed message: approval must name the reviewed plan revision>). Use the same helper as the verified-local guard. This error handling runs before decode, compare, readiness and any write. A refusal therefore changes no bytes or activity, publishes nothing, and keeps a pending SPEED timer, because cancelSpeedModeTimeout runs only after the write.

Keep everything else as it is:
- An explicit 0 for a stamp-less row is still accepted.
- null and malformed tokens still go through decodeSuppliedPlanRevision.
- A stale token still gets PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH.
- The stamp still travels in the daemonOwned argument.
- Unstamped history is never upgraded or backfilled. F04's existing "(L) durable approval authorization" tests pin this and must stay green unchanged.

Rewrite the approveTask comment that says ABSENCE is the only legacy opt-out, citing the rail. In packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts, change ONLY the two comments that call omission the legacy approval (the APPROVE_TASK case and the UPDATE_TASK drag route); there is no behavior change in that file. assertApprovalCapabilities stays as it is: a negotiated socket still gets its own negotiation message first. Do not touch StateManager.approveTask's signature.

Re-run the three test files: the flipped tests pass and the kept explicit-0 tests stay green.

UPDATE THE WIRE CONTRACT in docs/MCP_SERVER.md. Change only the sentences about omitted human-approval tokens:
- Around line 2909, "optional only for unnegotiated legacy clients ..." now says both routes require expectedPlanRevision from every client. An omission is refused with -32602 / INVALID_INPUT before any write. An explicit 0 still approves a stamp-less row.
- Around line 2913, the APPROVE_TASK request type makes expectedPlanRevision: number required. Make the UPDATE_TASK drag text match, wherever the doc describes it.
- Around line 2954, in the token-free approvals bullet, drop the unnegotiated omitted-token APPROVE_TASK and drag. Replace "stays accepted only until the human-approved deletion lands (CQ-F04b ...)" with a statement that it was deleted by CQ-F04b under the human-approved CQ-F rail. Keep the relaxed set_task_status clause, and do not rewrite the CQ-F05 clause beyond what its landed behavior requires.
docs/PLAN_APPROVAL_FRESHNESS.md and docs/SCHEMA.md belong to CQ-F12 (task-72184c65), the epic's docs sweep. Do not edit them; a comment on F12 records the stale line.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW (load adversarial-self-review), over this task's diff. Check each of the following.
- Is there any human route left that approves without a token? Cover APPROVE_TASK, the UPDATE_TASK drag, negotiated sockets, and unnegotiated sockets after a reconnect.
- Does any refusal write bytes, append activity, broadcast to another socket, cancel a SPEED timer or touch approvedPlanRevision?
- Are explicit 0 on a stamp-less row and stale-token PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH unchanged? Do null, '' and other malformed tokens still give INVALID_INPUT?
- Grep that state.approveTask still has exactly the two WS callers, and that relaxed set_task_status and SPEED/TURBO still bypass it.
- Does every rewritten pin cite the rail?
- Was the held-out acceptance file left untouched?
- Does the diff stay free of the project's globalRails forbidden patterns?
Fix anything you find. If any byte changed, re-run step 4's command and submit that fresh output.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Option 1, chosen: refuse the omission once, inside taskStore.approveTask. Both human /ws routes funnel into it, and nothing else calls it; relaxed set_task_status uses updateTask directly, and SPEED/TURBO use daemonOwned. So one guard covers APPROVE_TASK and the board drag, and leaves the token-free daemon producers with their owners, as the description requires.
Option 2, rejected: refuse in each WS route. That puts two guards in two places, and a third route could be added later without one.
Option 3, rejected: make StateManager.approveTask's parameter required in TypeScript. Vitest does not type-check tests, and both production callers already pass the argument, so it adds a file for no enforced benefit.
The client work was split into CQ-F04c (JetBrains) and CQ-F04d (VS Code), and the incidental test fixtures into CQ-F04e. All three are dependencies, so no supported client ever loses approval, and this row stays at 6 files.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: approveTask (state/taskStore.ts) already orders its checks status -> token decode/compare -> readiness -> single write, with cancelSpeedModeTimeout after the write, so a refusal placed before decode is automatically side-effect free. invalidInput('expectedPlanRevision', ...) is the existing helper; the WS layer serializes it to an ERROR frame whose context allowlist already includes expectedPlanRevision. I01 added assertApprovalCapabilities: for a negotiated socket it refuses omission with its own message before approveTask runs, and an unnegotiated socket (agreement undefined) reaches approveTask. Explicit 0 on a stamp-less row is distinct from omission and stays accepted (decodeStoredPlanRevision reads an absent stamp as 0).
